newsitem.title: GERMANY: LCE/LIFFE merger seen raising coffee futures trade.
newsitem.headline: LCE/LIFFE merger seen raising coffee futures trade.

text.p: The merger between the London International Financial Futures Exchange (LIFFE) and London Commodity Exchange (LCE) would bring long-term volume gains in coffee futures trade, said Clive Furness, director of business development at the LCE.
"It's a how long is a piece of string question, but yes -- it will happen," he said in response to questions at the F.O. Licht world coffee conference here.
"We have just finished putting long-term business plans together and two years down the line we will see success," he said.
The two exchanges were officially merged on Monday.
The business plans were aimed at optimising coffee futures' operators access and participation in the London markets and to generate added liquidity from other LIFFE floors, Furness said.
Growth would be achieved in the traditional LCE contracts and new products would be developed.
A reduction in exchange fees and infrastructure cost savings would stimulate interest in the LCE contracts.
